title: Control Plane Evidence Graph
assertions: every evidence chain must connect observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next loop
change and verifier refs must point to existing repository files or package directories
artifact evidence refs are names only and must stay redacted
evidence graph records explain why a loop exists without relying on narrative memory
frontend handoff decisions that change thread semantics must connect to the closed-loop claim that enforces them
cross-repository lifecycle observations must become owned open questions when this repository cannot safely change the runtime owner
evidence graph evidence must publish generated_at and expires_at and refresh on a schedule
evidence graph refresh evidence must expose workflow_file, cadence_minutes, and manual_refresh_command, and the workflow must upload the evidence artifact with strict if-no-files-found behavior
every evidence graph chain must cite at least one Loop Registry claim so reasoning routes cannot become orphan narrative records

chains.observation: Provider, smoke, load, performance, and release-readiness harness failures or stale partials could previously end as isolated artifacts.
chains.hypothesis: Redacted harness summaries or loop-owned stale-partial evidence can be transformed into closed-loop candidate records.
chains.decision: Harness failures and stale partial readiness evidence are promoted into closed-loop candidate artifacts by either the harnesspromotion sidecar or a loop-owned candidate producer; candidates still require claim binding, verifier, CI gate, redacted evidence, decision record, and evidence graph edge before adoption.

chains.observation: Redacted live workflow summaries could be reused after or exactly at their evidence expiry boundary, allowing stale harness output to create fresh closed-loop candidates.
chains.hypothesis: Stamping generated_at and expires_at in the redacted summary, then requiring generated_at < expires_at and now < expires_at in harness promotion, prevents stale observations from entering the closed-loop backlog.
chains.decision: Harness promotion now treats evidence freshness as a strict merge gate: malformed windows, zero-length windows, expired summaries, and exact-expiry summaries cannot produce closed-loop candidate evidence. The same gate applies after the testnet smoke switched from fixed provider fixtures to visible_runtime_acceptance summaries, and after the live principal proved assignable agents can lack daemon detail: optional v1 mutation warnings, v2 runtime-backed creation fallback, and product-mutation partial warnings are all captured in the same fresh redacted summary window, so dynamic live-principal runtime evidence cannot be promoted after expiry.

chains.observation: The live workflow evidence verifier only checked selected substrings, so generated_at, expires_at, redaction, and manifest evidence shape could drift while the provider acceptance harness still reported a passing freshness gate.
chains.hypothesis: Hashing the full generated manifest evidence and redacted deployment summary after pinning the clock and injected secret inputs makes the verifier fail on any unreviewed output-shape or redaction drift without changing runtime endpoint behavior.
chains.decision: Live workflow evidence behavior is now golden-locked before syntax target expansion: existing claim verifier names remain stable, while the verifier compares full SHA-256 outputs and still proves injected token/base URL values are absent.

chains.observation: tools/liveworkflowevidence owned provider-acceptance redaction and live workflow evidence but remained outside the syntax hash graph, so agents could not route AST-shape changes in that package to the provider acceptance semantic claim.
chains.hypothesis: After the live workflow evidence behavior is golden-locked, adding the package as a syntax hash target can connect all package files, relocation hashes, and physical constraints to the existing provider acceptance semantic hash without changing runtime behavior.
chains.decision: The live workflow evidence package is now syntax-hash tracked only after its behavior golden passed; repository syntax coverage rises while the target reports 100% package coverage, zero collisions, relocation mappings for every file hash, and zero physical-constraint violations.

chains.observation: The provider acceptance harness now declares visible_runtime_acceptance and daemon_runtime_snapshot observations, but the redacted smoke summary or loop manifest could omit structured daemon-bound assignable or creatable runtime agent coverage while still reporting generic contract coverage.
chains.hypothesis: Binding those observations to workflow source phrases, summary claims, machine-readable visible daemon-bound runtime acceptance, and the ai_thread_history loop identity lets agents see which provider/runtime paths and live v3 thread-history API surfaces were verified without reading raw live output or exporting secrets; legacy v1 mutation remains opportunistic because the live smoke principal may expose assignable agents without agent daemon bindings, while v2 attempts existing daemon-bound agents first, then runtime-based smoke-agent creation, and otherwise records an explicit product-mutation warning instead of failing contract/read smoke.
chains.decision: Provider acceptance evidence now exposes visible runtime acceptance through a dynamically selected or created daemon-bound agent when live seed data supports it, daemon runtime snapshot, and live v3 thread-history smoke coverage in the safe redacted summary path, while loop-registry evidence rejects observation/summary drift before merge. The live seed proved v1 and v2 can list assignable agents without daemon detail, so v1 mutation is skipped with an explicit warning when no daemon-bound candidate exists, v2 attempts runtime-backed smoke-agent creation as a fallback, and product mutation is explicitly warned as partial when the live principal has neither an assignable nor creatable daemon-bound agent.

chains.observation: Runtime settings now need a device-scoped daemon list because the singular device daemon endpoint intentionally returns only the preferred daemon. Without a live smoke check, the plural contract can be merged while staging remains on a build that only proves the singular endpoint. A development deploy smoke later proved a sharper mismatch: the singular `/devices/{device_id}/daemon` compatibility endpoint returned 200, while plural `/devices/{device_id}/daemons` returned 200 with no matching daemon row, so deploy smoke failed before profile thumbnail upload.
chains.hypothesis: Checking `/devices/{device_id}/daemons` in both scheduled testnet smoke and deploy smoke proves the generated plural client contract is present in the live API and returns at least one daemon for the selected device without changing existing singular endpoint behavior. If no profile-specific daemon rows are visible, the plural read model should include the same device read-model fallback used by the singular compatibility endpoint so clients and smoke do not disagree about whether the device has a daemon representation.
chains.decision: The plural daemon endpoint is a live product contract for runtime settings, not a replacement for the preferred singular daemon endpoint. Scheduled and deploy smoke call the plural endpoint after the singular endpoint and assert a `DeviceDaemonListResponse` scoped to the same device id, so deployment cannot be considered green while only the singular daemon route is verified. Development deploy smoke run 28806164797 showed singular 200 plus plural 200 without a matching daemon row, so the plural read model now falls back to the same device read-model daemon projection when no daemon rows are visible; this preserves endpoint shape, keeps the singular compatibility endpoint unchanged, and proves the fallback with `TestHTTPAIAgentClientDeviceDaemonsIncludesReadModelFallback`.

chains.observation: Claim semantic hashes can become self-referential if semantic_hash metadata values inside bound generated files are treated as semantic input.
chains.hypothesis: Normalizing semantic_hash metadata values before hashing preserves real statement, policy, verifier, and bound-file meaning changes while preventing evidence refresh metadata from becoming its own meaning change.
chains.decision: Semantic hash metadata is now hash-inert evidence metadata; claim hashes still move when semantic content or bound executable surfaces move.

chains.decision: Load/stress failures now have the same closed-loop promotion path as smoke failures: daily evidence refresh, redacted summary, candidate artifact, intake, and decision records.

chains.observation: The Notion QA completion-progress P0 still needed evidence that a completed AI Agent assignment cannot be made to look active again by late daemon progress. Existing stop-terminal tests covered user stop, but completed terminal state had no HTTP-level v2/v3/subscription/SSE replay proof. A live frontend report later showed the inverse edge: v3 history had the final answer after refresh, but the pre-refresh UI stayed running because clients subscribed to agent_thread_progress can miss terminal agent_work_status_changed events. A later Claude Code recurrence exposed the remaining delivery gap after terminal-progress fanout was added: the control-plane subscriber channel buffered 32 events and silently dropped every event on overflow, including terminal progress, so Claude's bursty progress could leave durable v3 state completed while the still-open client stream never received completion. Daemon executable knowledge already retains terminal reports until accepted and assigns SSE fanout ownership to control-plane, so the contradiction was inside control-plane delivery and its old claim that every live line reaches subscribers.
chains.hypothesis: Focused regression tests can prove the completed terminal path without changing endpoints: after assignment poll, running log, and assignment_completed, a late /thread-progress batch for the same assignment/thread/run must be rejected and must not leak into v2 threads, v3 history, active_thread_filters, or SSE replay. Terminal task action responses must fan out a progress-compatible terminal event; when a subscriber buffer is full that terminal event must displace buffered non-terminal progress, and a reconnect must synthesize one idempotent terminal replay event from a recent durable terminal thread if the event is absent. Structured stream lifecycle, overflow summary, priority-delivery, and replay-compensation logs can then distinguish provider completion, control-plane fanout pressure, and connection loss without recording credentials or message bodies.
chains.decision: The server side of the completed-but-still-progressing P0 now covers both terminal creation and terminal delivery: completed assignments reject late daemon progress, expose no active stream/filter residue, emit a progress-compatible terminal SSE event, prioritize that event over buffered progress when the 32-event subscriber channel is full, and reconstruct one recent missing terminal replay event from durable v3 thread state on subscription. Connection close reasons, fanout overflow summaries, terminal priority delivery, and replay compensation are logged without query credentials or message bodies. Claude Code remains responsible for reporting terminal outcome until accepted; control-plane is responsible for client SSE delivery and compensation. Product closure still requires a live post-deploy Claude recurrence showing the pre-refresh UI closes without manual reload.

loop.hypothesis: A compact evidence graph can make the development loop navigable by tools without asking an AI to read every narrative document.
loop.execute: Verify every chain has observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next-loop nodes; verify repository refs exist; generate this reader and publish graph evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on incomplete chains, duplicate ids, missing refs, stale generated docs, missing strict workflow evidence, or missing redaction on artifact evidence.
loop.retrospective: This makes the evidence loop itself inspectable: future agents can see why a loop exists, what changed, what verifies it, and what loop should run next.
